# Lab 12.13: Model Monitoring

## What We Are Going to Do
Check for training–serving skew and for drift between two time periods with BigQuery ML's monitoring functions.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Describe the training data.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT * FROM ML.DESCRIBE_DATA((SELECT * FROM lab12.v_income), STRUCT(10 AS top_k));</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] Create "serving" data that has shifted.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE lab12.serving_income AS
SELECT * REPLACE (age + 15 AS age, hours_per_week + 10 AS hours_per_week)
FROM lab12.v_income
WHERE MOD(ABS(FARM_FINGERPRINT(CAST(age AS STRING) || occupation)), 10) = 0;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[SQL] Check skew against the model's training data.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT input, metric, threshold, value, is_anomaly
FROM ML.VALIDATE_DATA_SKEW(MODEL lab12.income_bt, TABLE lab12.serving_income)
ORDER BY is_anomaly DESC, value DESC;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   `age` and `hours_per_week` are flagged.

4. **[SQL] Check drift between two tables.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT input, metric, value, is_anomaly
FROM ML.VALIDATE_DATA_DRIFT(
  (SELECT * FROM lab12.v_income),
  (SELECT * FROM lab12.serving_income),
  STRUCT(0.03 AS numerical_default_threshold))
ORDER BY value DESC;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **[CLI] Schedule the check.** Save the skew query as a daily scheduled query that writes to `lab12.skew_log`, so you can alert on new anomalies.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq mk --transfer_config --data_source=scheduled_query --target_dataset=lab12 \
  --display_name=daily_skew_check --schedule="every 24 hours" \
  --params='{"query":"SELECT CURRENT_DATE() AS run_day, * FROM ML.VALIDATE_DATA_SKEW(MODEL lab12.income_bt, TABLE lab12.serving_income)","destination_table_name_template":"skew_log","write_disposition":"WRITE_APPEND"}'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Skew | Serving vs training statistics |
| Drift | Data now vs data before |
| Flagged features | `age`, `hours_per_week` |
| Automation | Daily scheduled check |
